verses.1:1: The word of the Lord which came to Micah the Morashtite in the days of Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah, which he saw concerning Samaria and Jerusalem.
verses.1:2: Listen, all peoples, and let the earth pay attention, and its fullness; and let the Lord God be a witness against you, the Lord from His holy temple.
verses.1:3: For look, the Lord will go out from His place, and will come down, and will tread upon the high places of the earth.
verses.1:4: And the mountains will be consumed beneath Him, and the valleys will be split apart like wax before fire, and like waters that rush down headlong.
verses.1:5: All this is because of the crime of Jacob, and because of the sins of the house of Israel. What is the crime of Jacob? Is it not Samaria? And what are the high places of Judah? Is it not Jerusalem?
verses.1:6: And I will make Samaria like a heap of stones in a field when a vineyard is planted; and I will pull her stones down into the valley, and I will uncover her foundations.
verses.1:7: And all her carved images will be cut to pieces, and all her wages will be burned with fire, and I will bring all her idols to destruction, because they were gathered from the wages of a prostitute, and even to the wage of a prostitute they will return.
verses.1:8: Over this I will lament and wail; I will go stripped and naked; I will make a lamentation like that of dragons, and a mourning like that of ostriches,
verses.1:9: because her wound is hopeless, because it has come even to Judah; it has touched the gate of my people, even to Jerusalem.
verses.1:10: In Gath do not declare it; do not weep with tears; in the house of dust, sprinkle yourselves with dust.
verses.1:11: And pass on for yourselves, beautiful dwelling, put to shame with disgrace; she who dwells at the exit has not gone out; the neighboring house, which stood for itself, will receive lamentation from you.
verses.1:12: For she who dwells in bitterness has grown weak for what is good, because evil has come down from the Lord to the gate of Jerusalem.
verses.1:13: The uproar of a chariot of astonishment is for the inhabitant of Lachish; she is the beginning of sin to the daughter of Zion, because in you the crimes of Israel were found.
verses.1:14: Therefore she will give emissaries over the inheritance of Gath, houses of falsehood for a deception to the kings of Israel.
verses.1:15: I will yet bring an heir to you who dwell in Mareshah; the glory of Israel will come even to Adullam.
verses.1:16: Make yourself bald and shear your hair over the children of your delights; widen your baldness like an eagle, because they have been led away captive from you.
verses.2:1: Woe to you who devise what is useless and work evil on your beds! In the morning light they do it, because their hand is against God.
verses.2:2: And they coveted fields and took them by force, and seized houses; and they were defrauding a man and his house, a man and his inheritance.
verses.2:3: Therefore this is what the Lord says: "Look, I am devising evil against this family, from which you will not remove your necks, and you will not walk proudly, because it is a most evil time."
verses.2:4: In that day a proverb will be taken up against you, and a song will be sung with sweetness by those who say, "By devastation we have been laid waste; the portion of my people has been changed; how will he depart from me, when he returns to divide our regions?"
verses.2:5: Because of this there will not be for you anyone casting the cord of the lot in the assembly of the Lord.
verses.2:6: Do not speak, you who speak; it will not drip upon these; shame will not overtake them.
verses.2:7: The house of Jacob says, "Has the Spirit of the Lord been shortened, or are His thoughts like these?" Are not My words good with him who walks uprightly?
verses.2:8: And on the contrary, My people has risen up as an adversary. From off the tunic you have taken away the cloak, and those who were passing by innocently you have turned to war.
verses.2:9: You have driven out the women of My people from the house of their delights; from their little ones you have taken away My praise forever.
verses.2:10: Arise and go, because you do not have rest here; because of its uncleanness it will be corrupted with the worst decay.
verses.2:11: If only I were not a man having a spirit, and spoke falsehood instead! I will drip to you for wine and for drunkenness; and this people will be the one upon whom it is dripped.
verses.2:12: With gathering I will gather all of you, Jacob; I will bring together into one the remnant of Israel; I will place him together like a flock in a sheepfold, like a herd in the middle of the pens; they will make an uproar from the multitude of men.
verses.2:13: For he who opens the way will go up before them; they will divide, and pass through the gate, and go in through it; and their king will pass on before them, and the Lord at their head.
verses.3:1: And I said, "Listen, ruler of Jacob, and leaders of the house of Israel: is it not for you to know justice,
verses.3:2: you who hate good and love evil, who take their skins by force from off them, and their flesh from off their bones;
verses.3:3: who have eaten the flesh of my people, and flayed their skin from off them, and broken their bones, and cut them to pieces as in a cauldron, and like flesh in the middle of a pot?
verses.3:4: Then they will cry out to the Lord, and He will not hear them, and He will hide His face from them at that time, just as they acted wickedly in their devices."
verses.3:5: This is what the Lord says concerning the prophets who lead My people astray, who bite with their teeth and proclaim peace, and if anyone does not put anything in their mouth, they sanctify war against him:
verses.3:6: "Therefore there will be night for you instead of vision, and darkness for you instead of divination; and the sun will go down over the prophets, and the day will grow dark over them.
verses.3:7: And those who see visions will be put to shame, and the diviners will be put to shame; and all of them will cover their faces, because there is no answer from God."
verses.3:8: Nevertheless, I have been filled with the strength of the Spirit of the Lord, with justice, and with power, to declare to Jacob his crime, and to Israel his sin.
verses.3:9: Listen to this, rulers of the house of Jacob, and judges of the house of Israel, who detest justice and pervert all that is upright,
verses.3:10: who build Zion with bloodshed, and Jerusalem with iniquity.
verses.3:11: Her rulers judged for bribes, and her priests taught for a wage, and her prophets divined for money; and they rested upon the Lord, saying, "Is not the Lord in our midst? Evils will not come upon us."
verses.3:12: Because of this, on your account, Zion will be plowed like a field, and Jerusalem will be like a heap of stones, and the mountain of the temple will become the high places of forests.
verses.4:1: And it will be: in the last of the days the mountain of the house of the Lord will be prepared at the summit of the mountains, and lofty above the hills, and peoples will flow to it,
verses.4:2: and many nations will hasten and say, "Come, let us go up to the mountain of the Lord and to the house of the God of Jacob; and He will teach us concerning His ways, and we will go in His paths, for from Zion the law will go forth, and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem."
verses.4:3: And He will judge between many peoples, and He will rebuke strong nations even far away; and they will beat their swords into plowshares and their spears into hoes; nation will not take up sword against nation, and they will no longer learn to wage war.
verses.4:4: And each man will sit beneath his vine and beneath his fig tree, and there will be no one to frighten him, for the mouth of the Lord of hosts has spoken.
verses.4:5: For all the peoples will walk, each one in the name of his god; but we will walk in the name of the Lord our God, forever and beyond.
verses.4:6: "In that day," says the Lord, "I will assemble her who limps, and I will gather her whom I had cast out and her whom I had afflicted;
verses.4:7: and I will make her who limps into a remnant, and her who had been distressed into a mighty nation; and the Lord will reign over them on Mount Zion, from now on and forever."
verses.4:8: And you, cloudy tower of the flock of the daughter of Zion, even to you it will come, and the first authority will come, the kingdom of the daughter of Jerusalem.
verses.4:9: Now why are you constricted with grief? Do you have no king, or has your counselor perished, that pain has seized you like a woman in labor?
verses.4:10: Be in pain and strain, daughter of Zion, like a woman in labor, for now you will go forth from the city, and you will dwell in the country, and you will come all the way to Babylon; there you will be delivered, there the Lord will redeem you from the hand of your enemies.
verses.4:11: And now many nations have been gathered against you, who say, "Let her be stoned, and let our eye look upon Zion."
verses.4:12: But they themselves have not known the thoughts of the Lord, and have not understood His counsel, for He has gathered them like the hay of the threshing floor.
verses.4:13: Arise and thresh, daughter of Zion, for I will make your horn iron, and I will make your hooves bronze; and you will crush many peoples, and you will destroy their plunder for the Lord, and their strength for the Lord of the whole earth.
verses.4:14: Now you will be laid waste, daughter of a robber. They have laid a siege against us; with a rod they will strike the cheek of the judge of Israel.
verses.5:1: And you, Bethlehem Ephrathah, are very small among the thousands of Judah; from you will go forth for Me One who is to be ruler in Israel, and His going forth is from the beginning, from the days of eternity.
verses.5:2: Because of this He will give them up until the time when she who is in labor gives birth, and the remnant of His brothers will return to the sons of Israel.
verses.5:3: And He will stand and shepherd in the strength of the Lord, in the majesty of the name of the Lord His God; and they will return, for now He will be magnified to the ends of the earth.
verses.5:4: And this One will be peace: when the Assyrian comes into our land, and when he treads upon our houses, then we will raise up against him seven shepherds and eight leading men;
verses.5:5: and they will shepherd the land of Assyria with the sword, and the land of Nimrod with its lances; and He will deliver us from Assyria when he comes into our land, and when he treads within our borders.
verses.5:6: And the remnant of Jacob will be in the midst of many peoples like dew from the Lord, and like drops upon the grass, which does not wait for a man, and does not await the sons of men.
verses.5:7: And the remnant of Jacob will be among the nations, in the midst of many peoples, like a lion among the beasts of the forests, and like a young lion among flocks of sheep; and when it passes through, and tramples down, and seizes, there is no one to rescue.
verses.5:8: Your hand will be exalted over your foes, and all your enemies will perish.
verses.5:9: "And it will be in that day," says the Lord, "I will remove your horses from your midst, and I will wipe out your chariots.
verses.5:10: And I will destroy the cities of your land, and I will tear down all your strongholds; and I will remove sorceries from your hand, and there will be no divinations in you;
verses.5:12: and I will cause your carved images and your statues to perish from your midst, and you will no longer worship the works of your hands;
verses.5:13: and I will uproot your groves from your midst, and I will shatter your cities.
verses.5:14: And I will execute vengeance, in fury and in indignation, upon all the nations that have not listened."
verses.6:1: Hear what the Lord speaks: "Arise, contend in judgment against the mountains, and let the hills hear your voice."
verses.6:2: Let the mountains hear the judgment of the Lord, and the strong foundations of the earth; for the judgment of the Lord is with His people, and with Israel it will be adjudicated.
verses.6:3: My people, what have I done to you? Or how have I been burdensome to you? Answer Me.
verses.6:4: For I brought you out of the land of Egypt, and from the house of slaves I delivered you, and I sent before your face Moses, and Aaron, and Miriam.
verses.6:5: My people, remember, please, what Balak, king of Moab, planned, and what Balaam, son of Beor, answered him, from Shittim all the way to Gilgal, so that you might know the righteous acts of the Lord.
verses.6:6: What worthy thing should I offer to the Lord? Should I bend the knee to God on high? Should I offer to Him burnt offerings and year-old calves?
verses.6:7: Can the Lord be appeased with thousands of rams, or with many thousands of fat male goats? Should I give my firstborn for my wickedness, the fruit of my body for the sin of my soul?
verses.6:8: I will show you, man, what is good, and what the Lord requires from you: indeed, to practice justice, and to love mercy, and to walk carefully with your God.
verses.6:9: The voice of the Lord cries out to the city, and there will be salvation for those who fear Your name: hear, tribes, and who will approve of it?
verses.6:10: Still there is fire in the house of the wicked, treasures of iniquity, and a smaller measure full of wrath.
verses.6:11: Will I justify a wicked balance, and the deceitful weights of a pouch?
verses.6:12: By which its rich men have been filled with iniquity, and those dwelling in it were speaking falsehood, and their tongue is fraudulent in their mouth.
verses.6:13: And therefore I have begun to strike you with destruction because of your sins.
verses.6:14: You will eat, and you will not be satisfied, and your humiliation will be in your midst; and you will take hold, and you will not save, and those whom you do save, I will give to the sword.
verses.6:15: You will sow, and you will not reap; you will tread the olive, and you will not be anointed with oil; and new wine, and you will not drink wine.
verses.6:16: And you have kept the precepts of Omri, and every work of the house of Ahab, and you have walked in their desires, so that I might give you over to destruction, and those dwelling in it to hissing; and you will bear the reproach of My people.
verses.7:1: Woe to me, for I have become like one who gathers clusters of the vintage in autumn! There is no bunch of grapes to eat; my soul has desired early-ripe figs.
verses.7:2: The holy one has perished from the earth, and there is no upright one among people; all of them lie in wait in blood; a man hunts his brother to death.
verses.7:3: They call the evil of their hands good: the prince demands, and the judge is engaged in repayment; and the great man has spoken the desire of his soul, and they have thrown it into confusion.
verses.7:4: The one who is best among them is like a brier, and the one who is upright is like a thorn from a hedge. The day of your watch, your visitation has come; now will be their devastation.
verses.7:5: Do not believe a friend, and do not put confidence in a leader; from her who sleeps in your bosom, guard the gates of your mouth.
verses.7:6: For a son brings dishonor to his father, and a daughter rises up against her mother, a daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law; and the enemies of a man are those of his household.
verses.7:7: As for me, however, I will look to the Lord; I will await God, my Savior; my God will hear me.
verses.7:8: Do not rejoice over me, my enemy, because I have fallen; I will rise up when I sit in darkness; the Lord is my light.
verses.7:9: I will bear the anger of the Lord, because I have sinned against Him, until He judges my case and executes my judgment. He will lead me out into the light; I will see His righteousness.
verses.7:10: And my enemy will look on, and she will be covered with shame, she who says to me, "Where is the Lord your God?" My eyes will look upon her; now she will be for trampling like the mud of the streets.
verses.7:11: A day for your walls to be built; on that day the law will be far away.
verses.7:12: On that day one will come even to you from Assyria, and as far as the fortified cities, and from the fortified cities as far as the river, and from sea to sea, and from mountain to mountain.
verses.7:13: And the earth will become a desolation because of its inhabitants, and because of the fruit of their thoughts.
verses.7:14: Shepherd Your people with Your rod, the flock of Your inheritance, dwelling alone in a woodland, in the midst of Carmel. They will graze in Bashan and Gilead as in ancient days.
verses.7:15: According to the days of your going out from the land of Egypt, I will show him marvels.
verses.7:16: The nations will see and be put to shame over all their might. They will put their hand over their mouth; their ears will be deaf.
verses.7:17: They will lick the dust like serpents; like crawling things of the earth, they will be thrown into turmoil in their houses. They will dread the Lord our God, and they will fear You.
verses.7:18: Who, God, is like You, who takes away iniquity and passes over the sin of the remnant of Your inheritance? He will not send forth His fury any longer, because He desires mercy.
verses.7:19: He will turn back and have mercy on us; He will put down our iniquities, and He will cast all our sins into the depth of the sea.
verses.7:20: You will give truth to Jacob, mercy to Abraham, which You swore to our fathers from ancient days.

notes.1:8: The Vulgate reads spoliatus ("stripped") where the Hebrew has "barefoot," and renders the Hebrew desert creatures as draconum ("dragons"; Hebrew "jackals") and struthionum ("ostriches").
notes.1:10: Across 1:10-14 the Vulgate translates several Hebrew place names literally to preserve their wordplays, here rendering Beth-le-aphrah as in domo pulveris ("in the house of dust"), along with lacrimis ne ploretis ("do not weep with tears").
notes.1:11: Continuing its literal translation of town names, the Vulgate renders Shaphir as habitatio pulchra ("beautiful dwelling"), Zaanan as in exitu ("at the exit"), and Beth-ezel as domus vicina ("the neighboring house"), and similarly renders Maroth in 1:12 as in amaritudinibus ("in bitterness").
notes.1:14: The Vulgate has a third-person verb dabit ("she will give") with emissarios ("emissaries"), translates Moresheth-gath as hæreditatem Geth ("the inheritance of Gath"), and renders Achzib as domus mendacii ("houses of falsehood").
notes.2:1: The Vulgate renders the Hebrew idiom for having power in one's hand literally as quoniam contra Deum est manus eorum ("because their hand is against God").
notes.2:4: The Vulgate reads cum suavitate ("with sweetness") where the Hebrew expresses a bitter wail, and construes the final clauses as a question about the returning divider of their lands (quomodo recedet a me, cum revertatur, qui regiones nostras dividat?).
notes.2:11: The Vulgate renders this difficult verse as a first-person optative lament (Utinam non essem...), keeps the literal verb stillo ("drip," as in 2:6) for prophetic utterance, and reads ebrietatem ("drunkenness") for the Hebrew "strong drink."
notes.2:13: The Vulgate renders the Hebrew "breaker" as pandens iter ("he who opens the way") and has ingredientur per eam ("go in through it") where the Hebrew reads "go out through it."
notes.3:1: The Clementine Vulgate reads singular princeps Jacob ("ruler of Jacob") alongside plural duces ("leaders"), whereas 3:9 and 3:11 use plural principes.
notes.3:7: The Vulgate reads vultos suos ("their faces," a variant plural form of vultus) where the Hebrew specifies covering the mustache or upper lip.
notes.3:11: The Vulgate places the verbs in the past imperfect (judicabant, docebant, divinabant, requiescebant, "rested") where the Hebrew uses imperfective/present forms and "leaned."
notes.4:3: Vulgate ligones literally means 'hoes' or 'mattocks,' where the Hebrew has 'pruning hooks.'
notes.4:8: Vulgate nebulosa ('cloudy' or 'misty') interprets Hebrew ophel ('hill' or 'citadel') as a term for mist or darkness modifying 'tower.'
notes.4:9: Vulgate moerore contraheris ('are you constricted with grief') is a distinctly Vulgate rendering where the Hebrew reads 'do you cry aloud.'
notes.4:11: Vulgate Lapidetur ('Let her be stoned') is a distinctly Vulgate reading where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads 'Let her be profaned.'
notes.4:14: In the Vulgate (following the Hebrew chapter division), this verse ends chapter 4 rather than beginning chapter 5; filia latronis ('daughter of a robber') renders the Hebrew phrase 'daughter of troops.'
notes.5:3: Vulgate convertentur ('they will return' or 'they will be converted') reflects the root for turning back, differing from the Hebrew Masoretic Text ('they will dwell securely').
notes.5:5: Vulgate in lanceis ejus ('with its lances') stands where the Hebrew reads 'in its entrances.'
notes.5:10: In the Clementine Vulgate, this verse includes the clauses numbered as 5:11 in some editions, so the verse numbering proceeds directly from 5:10 to 5:12.
notes.5:13: Vulgate lucos tuos ('your groves') renders Hebrew Asherim (Asherah poles) as sacred groves.
notes.6:7: Vulgate in multis millibus hircorum pinguium ('with many thousands of fat male goats') is a distinctly Vulgate reading where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads 'with ten thousands of rivers of oil.'
notes.6:8: Vulgate Indicabo ('I will show,' first-person future) differs from Hebrew 'He has told,' and sollicitum ('carefully' or 'attentively') expresses conscientious watchfulness rather than 'humbly.'
notes.6:9: Vulgate salus erit timentibus nomen tuum ('there will be salvation for those who fear Your name') and tribus, et quis approbabit illud ('O tribes, and who will approve of it') reflect a distinctly Vulgate interpretation of a difficult Hebrew line.
notes.6:10: Vulgate Adhuc ignis ('Still there is fire') reads the Hebrew particle as the noun 'fire,' and irae plena ('full of wrath') stands where the Hebrew has 'accursed.'
notes.6:13: Vulgate coepi ('I have begun') translates the Hebrew verb from the root 'to begin' rather than from the homonymous root meaning 'to make sick' or 'strike grievously.'
notes.7:2: The Vulgate renders Hebrew herem as ad mortem ("to death") rather than "with a net," and uses the ablative in sanguine ("in blood") rather than "for blood."
notes.7:3: The Vulgate reads Malum manuum suarum dicunt bonum ("They call the evil of their hands good") and conturbaverunt eam ("they have thrown it into confusion"), differing from the Hebrew ("hands are on evil to do it well" and "they weave it together").
notes.7:11: The Vulgate renders Hebrew hoq as lex ("the law") rather than "boundary," giving longe fiet lex ("the law will be far away") rather than an extended border.
notes.7:12: The Vulgate translates Hebrew Matsor as civitates munitas ("the fortified cities") rather than a poetic name for Egypt, and preserves the indefinite singular verb veniet ("one will come").
notes.7:18: The Clementine Vulgate punctuates Deus as a vocative ("Who, God, is like You") and reads Non immittet ultra furorem suum ("He will not send forth His fury any longer"), where the Hebrew has "Who is a God like You" and "He does not retain His anger forever."
